label: EMULLM
description: Coordination, audio, transcription, and administration infrastructure for Codex/Copilot workers over durable JSONL event streams with HTTP/HTTPS/WS/WSS parity.
summary: Run the EMULLM server, review its transports, and open its administration console.

mailboxEndpoint.description: ws_collab-compatible mailbox directory served by the embedded EMULLM router (also answers at /emullm/mailbox/mailboxes); sibling routes /messages, /send share the base.

servicesEndpoint.description: Native EMULLM catalog of every HTTP and WebSocket service, including comments, parameters, request bodies, responses, reusable schemas, and the shared worker socket at /emullm/ws.

steps: Install the `emullm` package into the repository .venv.
Start the standalone server, or set EMULLM_PLUGIN_MODE=embedded to mount it in-process.
Open the administration console and confirm the transports answer.
Stop the standalone EMULLM server (or unset EMULLM_PLUGIN_MODE=embedded and stop the embedded mount).
This is a vendored nested project (its own .git) -- remove its directory entirely to uninstall it, or leave it and just disable scanning it (set scan: disabled in plugins.json).

plugin-init.description: Redirects /emullm to the Workspace Emulation Router plugin.

plugin-lifecycle.note: Runs in the runtimeModes.current selection. Standalone owns its server process; embedded mounts the router into Workbench. Changing modes takes effect on the next Workbench/API restart.

status.description: JSON worker/route/config state (see also /emullm/status for the HTML view).

services.description: Native service catalog with comments, parameter metadata, request schemas, responses, and reusable component schemas.

workerWebSocket.description: Single worker socket; optional worker_id and modelmasks query parameters identify and filter each connection without creating new paths.

plugin-endpoints.note: No HTTP route restarts or shuts down the process itself. /emullm/admin/reset clears persisted records (files/assistants/threads/events/mailbox storage) -- a data reset, not a process restart -- so it is deliberately not listed as 'restart' here.
